anya: Quick sync: proposing an adaptive trace lifecycle pilot to reduce cold storage and make old-trace debugging predictable. Short thread on policy, index, and billing.

kevin: TLDR of the policy?

anya: Keep full spans + index for 10d. After that run adaptive compression: for each trace compute a retention_hint = max(error_flag, latency_bucket, alert_tag). If hint==high -> keep full 30d. If medium -> compact per-request shard 90d. If low -> metrics-only 365d.

hema: How do we compute retention_hint cheaply at ingest?

jorge: Use existing fields: has_error boolean, max_span_ms, sampled_flag. A small bitmask compute is O(1). No extra lookups.

kevin: Query UX concerns: ops will expect find-by-request to always work.

anya: UX plan: when a query hits an archived trace return breadcrumb + retention status + rehydrate button. If trace was compacted, show top-op summary and error histogram.

hema: Rehydrate SLA?

anya: Default rehydrate ETA 30-90m. Incident-priority rehydrates in 5-20m. Support route requires justification and records a cost event.

jorge: Billing: attribute cold storage to billing_key in rollup proto. Charge rehydrates as a small per-op line item.

kevin: Metrics to watch during pilot: cold_storage_gb, rehydrate_rate, rehydrate_p95, percent_queries_served_by_compact, support_restore_tickets.

anya: Pilot: infra/adaptive-trace-lifecycle-382500. Staging + 5% prod for 2 weeks. Success: >=20% cold tier reduction and <=15% increase in mean trace-search latency. Kill-switch and circuit breaker prefabs included.

sre-bot: Pilot ticket created: infra/adaptive-trace-lifecycle-382500. Dashboards stubbed. Monitors: rehydrate_cost/hr and rehydrate_latency_p95.
